canonical_statement: For measurable events A_n in a probability space whose probability sums diverge, the probability of limsup A_n is at least the limsup of the squared partial probability sum divided by the double partial sum of pairwise-intersection probabilities.
domain_and_universes: Omega : Type u; MeasurableSpace Omega; probability measure mu; A : Nat -> Set Omega; Prop in universe 0
hypotheses: the finite partial sums of mu(A n) diverge to infinity
conclusion: limsup_n ((sum_{k<n} mu(A_k))^2 / sum_{i,j<n} mu(A_i intersect A_j)) <= mu(limsup_n A_n)
